scope: Proposition 5.3 (Uniform local conditional comparison) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE₃ limits for general weak random-bond Ising models” (preprints/Quenched-SLE3-limits-for-general-weak-random-bond-Ising-models-October-5-2026/general-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c693f39898f6f7d7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the array hypotheses above and (5.1). Fix a bounded polygonal window with a finite family T of corridor crossings, band circuits, or passage checks, strictly inside specified free buffers. Annular windows may have an inner and an outer free collar. Dilate the whole geometry by r → ∞ in lattice units. There is an exterior-independent measurable envelope Er(η) with EEr → 0, uniformly over translations and scale-grid positions, such that every level-zero conditional test-vector law is within Er(η) in total variation of a mixture of pure conditional test-vector laws on a still-buffered interior window. Consequently, if an event in the test vector has pure conditional probability at least c∗ > 0 under all exterior assignments after a sufficiently small fixed erosion of the buffers, its level-zero probability is at least any c < c∗, uniformly over exterior assignments, outside an environmental event of probability tending to zero. For a nearest-neighbor initial law, the event that this worst-boundary lower bound holds depends only on the bonds in the window and its incident layer.
